children: Japan’s headline annual inflation rate held at 1.9% in August 2026, remaining unchanged from July and hovering at its highest level since December 2025.
On a monthly basis, consumer prices edged up 0.1%, pacing noticeably slower than the upwardly revised 0.5% increase recorded in the prior month.

The core consumer price index (CPI), which excludes fresh food but includes energy, rose 1.7% Y/Y in August. The reading represents a slight deceleration from July’s six-month high of 1.8% and came in just below consensus forecasts of 1.8%.
Core CPI has now remained below the Bank of Japan’s 2% target for eight consecutive months, as government fuel subsidies helped blunt broader price pressures driven by elevated global oil costs.
Food inflation also showed signs of easing, rising 3.1% Y/Y in August compared to 3.5% in July, marking the softest annual gain for the category since July 2024.
